When your child says "I want a puppy"

When your child begs for a pet, you feel happy but also worried. They love the idea at first, but caregiving like feeding and walks is easy to keep putting off.

Caregiving is hard to teach with words. But when a child first experiences a moment where "it won't happen unless I do it" through a story, they naturally feel the weight of responsibility.

Curious about the plot of this pet care storybook? Explore the lessons of the pet care storybook along with the illustrations. Meet the key scenes of the pet care story too. Read the pet care storybook together with your child and talk about it. We've woven together many stories about 43. Feed and Pet, My Friend Dubu!, including a puppy care storybook, a responsibility storybook, and a respect-for-life storybook.
content.caption: Caregiving is learned in the moments when it won't happen unless I do it.

content.alt: 43. Feed and Pet, My Friend Dubu! - Why responsibility and respect for life matter
content.text:
Why responsibility and respect for life matter

Caring for a pet teaches a child how to take responsibility for "a being that needs me." In the process of providing food and water and checking for sore spots, a child learns both thoughtfulness and diligence.

Above all, the sense that life is precious and that there is a being who depends entirely on me makes a child's heart deep and warm. This is a strength that carries straight over into human relationships too.
content.caption: Caring for a being that needs me grows thoughtfulness and diligence.

content.alt: 43. Feed and Pet, My Friend Dubu! - The story of Hori learning to care for Dubu
content.text:
The story of Hori learning to care for Dubu

In "Feed and Pet, My Friend Dubu!", Hori gets caught up in play and keeps putting off feeding Dubu. Only when Hori sees Dubu drooping weakly with hunger does Mom's words hit hard: "Dubu can only live if you take care of him."

Hori quickly brings food and water, goes for walks, checks Dubu's paws, and becomes a caring friend. At night Hori holds Dubu close and whispers, "From now on I'll take good care of you every day." Together with Hori, your child learns the responsibility and love of caregiving.
content.caption: From now on I'll take good care of you every day — a caring friend was born.

content.alt: 43. Feed and Pet, My Friend Dubu! - Practicing caregiving together at home
content.text:
Practicing caregiving together at home

As you read the story, ask "How do you think Dubu felt when he was hungry?" to help your child imagine the animal's feelings. Empathy is the first step of caregiving.

Then give your child a small role they can handle, like changing the water, giving food, or coming along on a walk. When they do well, praise them with "He got healthy thanks to you!" and your child will remember responsibility as something to be proud of. Playing caregiver with a toy puppy is good practice too.
content.caption: Give a small caregiving role to make responsibility something to be proud of.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions

Q. How do I let my child care for a pet?

A. Teach them to cherish life through feeding and petting, as if it were play. Even a small caregiving task, when entrusted and praised, grows both responsibility and warmth.

Q. How does a pet care storybook help?

A. By seeing the main character treasure their animal friend, your child learns to respect life too. A pet care storybook warmly conveys the joy and responsibility of caregiving.

Q. How can a child who is scared of animals get comfortable with them?

A. Rather than forcing them closer, let them get used to it slowly at their own pace. Watching from afar and then approaching little by little builds experiences that reduce fear.
